title: Black Holes are about Quantum Information
abstract: We review and analyse quantum information-theoretic approaches to black hole evaporation that purport to bring us closer to a resolution of the black hole information paradox. Our focus is on the Page-time paradox and on the contribution of the Hayden-Preskill model to understanding information release under the assumption of unitary evaporation. In this model, the black hole is taken to be a finite-dimensional quantum system whose dynamics can be represented by a quantum circuit, and its information-processing and communication abilities are studied. We identify the assumptions underlying this modelling and highlight two key features, fast scrambling dynamics and entanglement as a resource, that underpin the information release in the model. We argue that this reasoning exemplifies a broader change in how information is used in black hole physics, in which quantum information theory now provides a useful operational modelling framework. This application avoids earlier philosophical objections insofar as it is not based on epistemic ignorance and does not regard information as a substance. This line of reasoning has become central to the debate and, as such, warrants greater attention from the philosophy of physics community.
summary: This paper reviews quantum information-theoretic approaches to the black hole information paradox, focusing on the Hayden-Preskill model. It argues that treating black holes as quantum circuits allows for an operational understanding of information release, highlighting fast scrambling and entanglement as key mechanisms. This shifts the focus from philosophical debates to a concrete, computational modeling framework.
main_problem: The paper addresses the black hole information paradox, specifically focusing on the Page-time paradox, by analyzing how quantum information theory can resolve the apparent loss of information during black hole evaporation.
main_result: The analysis shows that modeling black holes as quantum circuits, utilizing concepts like fast scrambling and entanglement as a resource, provides a useful operational framework for understanding information release under unitary evolution.
method: The authors review and analyze quantum information-theoretic approaches, particularly focusing on the Hayden-Preskill model, which treats the black hole as a quantum channel.
model_or_system: The system under study is a black hole, which is modeled as a finite-dimensional quantum system whose dynamics are represented by a quantum circuit. The framework relies on the assumption of unitary evolution.
key_observables: Black hole entropy ($S_{BH}$), information release dynamics, and the time scale for information recovery.
important_parameters: The area of the black hole horizon ($A_{BH}$), and the assumption of unitarity.
main_assumptions: The central assumption is the 'central dogma' of unitarity, treating the black hole as an ordinary quantum system, which the authors note is a necessary modeling assumption for tractability.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the information controversy, analyzes the Hayden-Preskill model using quantum information tools, and discusses the implications of treating black holes as quantum computational systems.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, abstract framework using quantum information tools (like those used in QEC) to model complex, non-equilibrium quantum processes in extreme gravity regimes, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems theory.
